meta.title: Chipotle: Traffic Came Back, the Stock Didn't
meta.dek: Chipotle beat on traffic for the third quarter running and missed on margin, and the stock rebounded 16% from a three-year low. Is $31.89 a recovery or a pause in a brand that has lost its edge?
meta.price_note: Oct 30, 2026 close, matched on Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis
meta.type: Company-operated fast-casual restaurants (unit: restaurant; AUV and restaurant-level margin)
meta.stage: Mature compounder in a traffic reset

verdict.sentence: A debt-free restaurant compounder with 7,000 locations of runway delivered a third quarter of positive traffic and a margin miss; the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, so the price is fair-to-full until the two-year traffic stack turns and price catches beef.
verdict.breaks_if: Q4 transactions fall short of the +1.5% the first test needs (the guide implies about +0.5%) and the 2027 guide implies a restaurant margin under 24%. Then the 2026 recovery was price, and 10 points move from the Base to the Bear.

call: Chipotle's third quarter answered the question the stock was asking and raised another. Comps were +2.1% against a +1% guide, transactions grew 0.8% against −0.8%, and the stock gained 16% in a week from a three-year low. But restaurant margin was 23.3% against my 24.0% bar, the fourth quarter is guided just under 22%, and October softened. The market is right that traffic is back and too quick to forget that price now only matches inflation, with 2027 inflation guided low to mid single digits. At $31.89 the price needs EPS growth of about [[Priced-in.cagr]] to earn 9% and implies only [[implied_bear]] Bear odds; I assign 30%. My Base caps the restaurant margin at 24% and earns [[Base.return]] a year; the weighted case earns [[pw_return]], short of 13% and now below the [[compounding]] the business compounds at a flat multiple, because the multiple falls from today's 30× to 24×. No debt, 350 openings a year and about 60% second-year cash-on-cash returns make this a business to own at [[entry]], not at $32.

tests.claim: That the traffic recovery is a turn, not a compare (Q4 leg).
tests.test: Q4 transactions ≥+1.5% against −3.2% in the Q4 release (February), so the two-year transaction stack improves again. The Q3 leg passed (+0.8% against −0.8%). The Q4 comp guide of about +2% with about 3% of price implies transactions near +0.5%.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]**, entry [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That restaurant margin stabilizes once price matches inflation.
tests.test: Q4 restaurant-level margin at least 21.8% (guide: just under 22%) and an FY2027 guide, or first-half 2027 margin, consistent with at least 24%.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]]; the Base margin cap drops from 24% to 23%.

tests.claim: That new units are not eating the old ones.
tests.test: trailing-12-month AUV at or above $3.10M in the FY2026 10-K (February; Q3: $3.106M), and year-two cash-on-cash returns still about 60% for the 2025 class.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the $4M AUV goal comes out of the Bull.

return_math.epv: ≈$12–14 per share: five-year average owner earnings of ≈$1.3B (FY2021–25), or FY2025's $1.47B, capitalized at 9% with no growth, plus $1.0B of cash, on 1.27B shares. About 58% of today's price pays for growth. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits above EPV because it keeps unit growth and buybacks while EPS goes nowhere.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs ≈10% nominal (≈7.5% real) revenue growth for five years from $13B; for companies of $10–25B, roughly a quarter sustain ≥7.5% real. Plausible, given visible unit growth. The Base's 8% nominal is in line with the unit pipeline alone.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing at year ten: 7,000 North American restaurants is about a decade of openings at 350 a year, plus international. The exit multiple is not doing the work in the Base, which ends at today's 24×.
